clue.text: Tradesman intended to support Red Cross hospital

indicators.note: the intended word props up the other letters by holding them inside itself

parts.note: meant is the past tense of mean, to intend
R is a standard abbreviation for red
C is the abbreviation for cross, as in RC for Red Cross
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who planned to back a Red Cross hospital with donations.
explanation.walkthrough: To support normally means to sit beneath, but here the intended word wraps round the abbreviations for Red Cross hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is someone who buys and sells goods, a trader.

clue.text: Setter's meal is said to be huge

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me, so the setter's meal is my tea

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler boasting that their dinner was enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is the evening meal in much of Britain; spoken quickly, my tea sounds like MIGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty can mean very large or imposing in size, a synonym of huge.

clue.text: Run to get English books for a student, available for a fee

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
E is the abbreviation for English
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
taken as written
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: Popping out to fetch English textbooks for a student, which can be hired rather than bought.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car. The definition is adjectival: a rental car is one available for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental item is one hired out for payment rather than sold outright.

clue.text: Harry has artists brought in

indicators.note: the artists are brought inside, so one word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAS

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry hiring a team of painters.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a man's name, but it is the verb to harry. RA (Royal Academician) is a standard abbreviation for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or attack repeatedly, the same as harass.

clue.text: Going out tonight in new American city

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another
going out suggests letters dispersed and rearranged as they leave

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new
AM is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An invitation to a night out in some new city in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at an American city, but Nottingham is in the English Midlands; American only supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is a city in the East Midlands of England, home of the Robin Hood legend.

clue.text: Regulate commercial fair

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
just means fair or equitable

explanation.surface: A call to oversee the rules of trade fairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Commercial looks like an adjective for fair, but here it is the noun meaning an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust a mechanism is to regulate or set it correctly.

clue.text: Doctor agonised to identify illness

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried physician agonising over pinning down what is wrong with a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the person doing the identifying, but it is a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to determine the nature of a disease from its symptoms.

clue.text: Confident of UN help after RAF debacle

indicators.note: after places the word for help behind the air force letters rather than before them

parts.note: taken as written, the United Nations

indicators.note: a debacle is a shambles, so these letters end up in disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
aid is help

explanation.surface: Feeling secure about United Nations support after an air force disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force; its jumbled letters sit in the middle, with help placed after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unafraid has no fear, so is bold and self-assured.

clue.text: Directed great play and empty theatre filled at last

indicators.note: play suggests letters moving freely and being reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, so only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of theatre

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of filled

explanation.surface: A director's great show, and an empty theatre that finally fills up.
explanation.walkthrough: Directed and play suggest the stage, but play signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Targeted means aimed or pointed at something, as directed efforts are.

clue.text: Produce information on drug (speed)

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is ecstasy
rate is speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: A request to produce facts about the drug known as speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed looks like the name of the drug, but it is just a synonym for rate. Gen is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to bring it into being, to produce it.

clue.text: Arab goes out carrying street guide to find market

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other
going out suggests the letters wandering off and returning in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
an A-Z is a London street atlas

explanation.surface: A traveller heads out clutching a map to locate the souk.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is the classic book of street maps of London and other British cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market, especially an oriental one with many stalls.

clue.text: Craft returning to North Pole gets repair for rivet

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for craft is read backwards

parts.note: art is craft or skill
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the south pole, one of the compass poles
to fix is to repair

explanation.surface: A boat coming back to the Arctic needing mending.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft and North Pole suggest a polar voyage; Pole is only S, and rivet is a verb, as in riveting attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix someone is to hold them motionless with fascination, just as to rivet them.

clue.text: Mum's sister doesn't begin to regret being unfaithful

indicators.note: a word that doesn't begin has lost its opening letter

parts.note: your mother's sister is your aunt
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An aunt who refuses to start feeling sorry about her infidelity.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNT loses its first letter to give UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue can mean disloyal, as in a lover untrue to a partner.

clue.text: March in favour of surrendering territory

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a cession is the formal handing over of land

explanation.surface: A protest march supporting giving up land.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month or a protest; it is the noun for an orderly parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession is a line of people moving forward in order, a march.

clue.text: Cruel gags about soldiers and heartless riddle are offensive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another
cruel treatment knocks things out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve

explanation.surface: Nasty jokes about the army and pointless puzzles cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddle here is the gardener's sieve, not a puzzle, and heartless takes out its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive and aggressive both describe hostile, attacking behaviour.

clue.text: Artist gets second trophy, including money, by recycling rubbish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside the trophy word

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

indicators.note: recycling sends something back round, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A runner-up artist wins prize money for a work made of recycled junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Money gives L from the pound sign, which comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor is an artist who carves or models three-dimensional works.

clue.text: Instrument for Clinton and Bird?

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument
Bill Clinton, the US president

explanation.surface: Asking what instrument suits Clinton, who famously played the saxophone, and someone called Bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird reads like a surname, as with jazz saxophonist Charlie Bird Parker, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbill is a tropical bird with a large curved beak topped by a casque.

clue.text: Get together to see lambs frolicking

indicators.note: frolicking animals leap about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet up and watch the spring lambs skipping about.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather in one place, to come together as a group.

clue.text: Bad tempered person in the graveyard?

definitions.text: Bad tempered person in the graveyard?

parts.note: the plain reading: a grumpy, irritable person
the setter's reading: a graveyard is a plot of land full of crosses marking graves

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: split the word into its two parts and it describes a churchyard plot of crosses, while the whole word is an old-fashioned term for a grouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an informal, slightly dated name for a cross, grumpy person.

clue.text: Explore London area of Bow

parts.note: SE is south-east, a London postal area
a bow is a curved arch

explanation.surface: Investigating the East London district of Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a real area of East London, which makes it look like part of a place name; it is the curved shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To search a place is to look through it thoroughly, to explore it.

clue.text: Urges simple correction

indicators.note: a correction changes what is there, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushing for an easy fix to a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, matching urges.

clue.text: Not even I try extremes of eccentricity

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of try

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to be balanced by trying out every extreme of strange behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremes looks as if it belongs with eccentricity, but it acts on try, and of is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a strange trait or peculiarity, a quirk of eccentric behaviour.

clue.text: Hang on to underwear that is removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so those letters come off the longer word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Clinging to one's underclothes after taking them off.
explanation.walkthrough: LINGERIE drops its final IE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on, to hang on rather than leave.

clue.text: Valued quarter horse brings in million Euro

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so letters are inserted

parts.note: east is one quarter of the compass
a steed is a horse
M is the abbreviation for million
E is the abbreviation for euro

explanation.surface: A prized quarter horse fetching a million euros at sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter horse is a real American breed, but quarter is one compass point here, kept apart from horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means highly regarded, valued and respected.

clue.text: Attempt to keep a pound in a hat!

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so other letters go within

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Trying to stash a pound coin inside one's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points up the silly picture of hiding cash under a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and an indented crown.

clue.text: Old PM from country bordered by Germany and Italy

indicators.note: a thing bordered by others has them at its edges, so it sits inside

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
Israel is a country
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A former prime minister from a nation between Germany and Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a European country such as Switzerland or Austria; the country is Israel, framed by D and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: Turn to Queen and wave

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Turning to face the Queen and waving at her.
explanation.walkthrough: Wave looks like a gesture at the monarch, but it is the noun for a sea swell.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a long, heavy wave that rolls in towards the shore.

clue.text: Honestly! Distribute letters in private

indicators.note: distributing the letters deals them out again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated person telling someone to hand out mail discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: Honestly! reads as an exclamation of exasperation, but it is the fodder, and letters means its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly means doing it secretly, out of sight of others.
